title: Figures with their provenance
jupyter: python3

Each figure below sits in a tabset: the figure, then its lineage as chronex recorded it. A step
is one node, however many times it ran; hover a step for its parameters, code version and
flags. The toy workflow behind these figures runs twice: once cleanly, and once with four
planted mistakes, so the two lineages can be compared.

```{python}
#| include: false
# Run the toy workflow twice, into work/clean and work/faulty (with its planted mistakes).
import os
import subprocess
import sys
from pathlib import Path

DOCUMENT = Path.cwd()
drive = (DOCUMENT / "../toy-workflow/drive.py").resolve()
for name, faults in (("clean", []), ("faulty", ["--faults"])):
    if not (DOCUMENT / "work" / name).exists():
        command = [sys.executable, drive, "decorator", f"work/{name}", *faults]
        subprocess.run(command, check=True, cwd=DOCUMENT)


def workspace(name: str) -> None:
    """Run the next cells where that run of the workflow wrote its records."""
    os.chdir(DOCUMENT / "work" / name)
```

## A clean run

The heat capacity curves come from the toy workflow's last step, `plot`. Every step completed,
and every input is accounted for: nothing is flagged.

```{python}
import chronex.quarto as cq

workspace("clean")
cq.figure("results/cv.png", caption="Heat capacity of the toy model", label="cv-clean")
```

## A run with mistakes

The same figure from the run with planted mistakes:

- a labelling job failed, but its output was collected anyway;
- a collected file was edited by hand;
- the fit read a config file it did not declare;
- the model was refitted halfway through the Monte Carlo scans.

Flagged steps are coloured, and their tooltips say what is wrong.

```{python}
workspace("faulty")
cq.figure("results/cv.png", caption="Heat capacity, from the run with mistakes", label="cv")
```

## A figure made in the document

This one is drawn here, in the cell, from the run with mistakes: `cq.make_figure` records the
cell as a step, so its lineage joins the pipeline's.

```{python}
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np

with cq.make_figure("figures/energy.png", caption="Energy against temperature") as s:
    curves = np.genfromtxt(s.input("results/curves.csv"), delimiter=",", names=True)
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(6, 3.5))
    for seed in np.unique(curves["seed"]):
        rows = curves[curves["seed"] == seed]
        ax.plot(rows["temperature"], rows["energy"], label=f"seed {seed:g}")
    ax.set(xlabel="temperature", ylabel="energy per site")
    ax.legend(frameon=False)
    Path("figures").mkdir(exist_ok=True)
    fig.savefig("figures/energy.png", dpi=150, bbox_inches="tight")
    plt.close(fig)
```
